name: Ransomware Disrupts Manufacturing
description: A financially motivated actor encrypts manufacturing and business systems, interrupting production and triggering recovery, notification, and customer-impact costs.
assumptions: Recovery takes 3–12 production days.
Cyber insurance recoveries are excluded.
A material data-theft claim is a secondary loss.

name: Business Email Compromise
description: An attacker impersonates an executive or supplier and induces finance staff to redirect a high-value payment.
asset: Treasury payments and supplier master data
assumptions: Only attempts reaching payment-authorized staff are counted.
Bank recovery is reflected in primary-loss estimates.
Regulatory action is unlikely but possible.

name: Cloud Document Exposure
description: A configuration or sharing error exposes regulated design, quality, or customer documents to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Exposure must include sensitive content to become a loss event.
Primary loss includes forensics and review.
Secondary loss includes customer claims and regulatory response.

name: Third-Party Logistics Outage
description: A cyber incident at a logistics provider prevents inbound materials or outbound medical-component shipments.
assumptions: The event lasts 2–10 business days.
Alternate carriers provide limited capacity.
Secondary loss includes service credits and customer attrition.

name: Shadow AI Data Leakage
description: An employee submits confidential product, quality, or customer data to an unapproved generative AI service.
asset: Product designs, quality records, and customer information
effect: Loss of confidentiality and contractual breach
assumptions: Only submissions containing material confidential data are loss events.
Provider retention and model-training terms vary.
Secondary losses include IP and customer-contract claims.

name: Departing Engineer Takes Design IP
description: An engineer leaving for a competitor exfiltrates proprietary component designs and process documentation before their access is revoked.
asset: Component designs and manufacturing process IP
assumptions: Only departures with access to material design IP are counted.
Primary loss covers investigation, legal action, and lost development advantage.
Secondary loss includes customer-contract exposure if designs reach a competitor.

name: OT Network Intrusion Halts Production
description: An attacker pivots from IT into the operational technology network; production is stopped while control systems are validated as safe before restart.
asset: Plant OT/ICS network and production line controllers
threat: Targeted intruder reaching the OT network
assumptions: Any confirmed OT intrusion forces a shutdown until controllers are revalidated.
Restart requires quality revalidation of in-process medical components.
Secondary loss covers customer penalties and expedited-shipping recovery costs.

name: Compromised Vendor Software Update
description: A trusted vendor's signed software update ships with malicious code, giving an attacker a foothold across the systems where it is installed.
assumptions: A threat event is a malicious update reaching a product we run.
Vulnerability reflects the chance the update is installed before the compromise is disclosed.
Primary loss covers enterprise-wide investigation, rebuild, and downtime.

name: Customer Portal Account Takeover
description: Credential-stuffing operators replay passwords leaked from other services against the distributor ordering portal and take over customer accounts.
asset: Distributor ordering portal and customer accounts
effect: Account takeover, fraudulent orders, and customer notification
assumptions: A loss event is a campaign that takes over at least one active customer account.
Primary loss covers fraud reversal, forced resets, and incident handling.
Secondary loss includes customer attrition and contractual notification duties.

name: Unpatched Internet-Facing System Breach
description: An opportunistic attacker exploits a known vulnerability in an internet-facing application before the patch is applied, reaching regulated quality and customer records.
threat: Opportunistic attacker scanning for known vulnerabilities
assumptions: A threat event is a critical vulnerability exposed to the internet before patching.
Vulnerability reflects the chance it is exploited within the patch window.
Secondary loss includes regulatory response and customer claims.
